Chapter 3: Building the Right Team Before Setting the Course
Once you’ve got humble, determined leadership at the core, what comes next? It’s all about people. The most successful organizations don’t start with a grand strategy or a big, bold vision. No—they focus first on making sure the right people are on board, and just as importantly, that the wrong people aren’t. Only after that do they choose the direction they’ll take.
Imagine you’re getting ready for a long journey. Before you even think about where the bus is headed, you want to make certain you’ve got the right folks on the bus, the wrong ones off, and everyone sitting exactly where they belong. That image really drives home how people decisions should always come before strategy decisions.
Now, why does this sequence matter so much? Well, when you’ve got the right people, you can handle just about any challenge that comes your way. Plans can change, and strategies might shift, but a strong team will adapt and keep moving forward. These are the folks who don’t need a manager breathing down their necks or constant pep talks—they’re self-motivated, flexible, and genuinely care about the organization’s success.
On the flip side, if the wrong people are sitting in key seats, even the most brilliant plan is likely to fall flat. No amount of training, rewards, or close supervision can make up for a poor fit or lack of real commitment. Taking the step to remove someone who isn’t right for the team isn’t about being harsh—it’s about being honest and rigorous. In fact, it’s actually an act of respect—both to the individual and the whole organization—because everyone deserves a chance to thrive in the right role.
And this isn’t just something for top leadership to worry about. It matters at every level. The best organizations create a culture where talent, character, and values matter much more than just what’s on someone’s résumé. They don’t settle; they’re relentless about finding the right people, and they’re not afraid to make tough calls if that’s what it takes to keep standards high.
So, what does this look like in practice? Here are a few steps you can take:
First, put character and values at the top of your list—way above skills or past experience.
Second, if someone’s not a good fit, move quickly but always be fair and respectful.
Third, make sure people are in roles where their natural strengths can really shine.
And finally, create an environment where your best people want to stay and keep contributing.
When you start with people, you lay down a solid foundation for everything else. With the right team, you’re ready to tackle obstacles, adapt to whatever comes next, and aim for real greatness.
Up next, we’ll look at how to build a culture where truth is valued, and tough realities are faced head-on.
